p01.why: A class that declares a constructor cannot have a non-static data member named after the class.

p02.why: A member function cannot have the name of the class.

p03.why: S is standard-layout, so a pointer to s converts to a usable pointer to its first member and back.

p04.why: A non-static data member cannot have a placeholder type such as auto.

p05.why: A non-static data member cannot be register.

p06.why: Data members have increasing addresses in declaration order, whatever their access.

p07.why: A data member and a member function cannot share a name.

p08.why: A non-static data member can have the class name when the class declares no constructor.

p09.why: A default member initializer cannot use parentheses.

p10.why: A member function that is not volatile cannot be called on a volatile object.

p11.why: The members of the anonymous union are members of Value, so v.i names one.

p12.why: Overloads with the same parameters must all have ref-qualifiers or none; GCC 16 accepts the declarations and the other compilers reject them.

p13.why: A static member initializer is not a place where S is complete, so sizeof(S) is not valid there.

p14.why: A function with an explicit object parameter cannot be static.

p15.why: An unscoped enumerator cannot have the name of the class.

p16.why: operator() and operator[] can be static, and operator[] can take two parameters.

p17.why: The address of a member function with an explicit object parameter is an ordinary function pointer, called with the object first.

p18.why: A member function of a local class can name the static variables of the function.

p19.why: A const static member of enumeration type can have a constant initializer in the class.

p20.why: A member function declared in the class can be defined outside with a qualified name.

p21.why: Member access needs a complete class, and Gauge is only declared.

p22.why: A const member function cannot change a data member that is not mutable.

p23.why: A member function that is not const cannot be called on a const object.

p24.why: An unnamed member of class type other than an anonymous union is not valid, and Clang and GCC reject it under -pedantic-errors.

p25.why: The empty base subobject can share the object's address, and the specification does not say it must; the program expects the shared address, which I predict.

p26.why: The address of a standard-layout object equals the address of its first data member.

p27.why: A member function of a local class must be defined inside the class.

p28.why: A class nested in a class with no name cannot have a static data member.

p29.why: A member function must be called or have its address taken with &S::f; s.f alone is not valid.

p30.why: A reference member cannot be mutable.

p31.why: A member function of a local class cannot name an automatic variable that is not a constant.

p32.why: A default argument sees the class as complete, so it can use a later member.

p33.why: A static member function cannot have a cv-qualifier.

p34.why: The size of an empty class is 1 on every compiler in the matrix.

p35.why: A local class cannot have a member template.

p36.why: this has type S* with the cv-qualifiers of the member function.

p37.why: A member function defined in its class is inline, so both units can define it.

p38.why: A function with an explicit object parameter cannot have a cv-qualifier.

p39.why: A class with no name cannot have a static data member.

p40.why: The operand of noexcept sees the class as complete, so g can be named before its declaration.

p41.why: = 0 is allowed only on a virtual member function.

p42.why: A static data member that is not const, inline, or constexpr cannot have an initializer in the class.

p43.why: A const static int member with an initializer is a constant usable as an array bound.

p44.why: A member can be a pointer to the incomplete class.

p45.why: A member of an anonymous union cannot have the name of the class.

p46.why: A static data member can have its own class type, defined after the class.

p47.why: A static member cannot be mutable.

p48.why: A function with an explicit object parameter cannot be virtual.

p49.why: The static data member has one definition in the program, shared by both units.

p50.why: The class must declare a member function before an outside definition.

p51.why: A static member function can be called through the class name or an object.

p52.why: A member function body sees members declared later.

p53.why: An inline static data member is one object defined in the class, so both units see the same address.

p54.why: A const member function can change a mutable member.

p55.why: A local class cannot have a static data member.

p56.why: The object of the call initializes the explicit object parameter, by value or by reference.

p57.why: An explicit object parameter must belong to a member function or a lambda.

p58.why: A non-static data member cannot be extern.

p59.why: Binding a reference uses the address of k, which has no definition outside the class, so the linker fails.

p60.why: self and the second parameter each copy g, and next() adds one more, so count is 3.

p61.why: A nested class cannot have the name of the class.

p62.why: A local class with member functions defined inside works like any class.

p63.why: Nested classes, aliases, and enumerators are named outside as Outer::name.

p64.why: The same member function cannot be declared twice, also if one is static.

p65.why: A function with an explicit object parameter has no this.

p66.why: A static member function cannot use this.

p67.why: A local class can read a constexpr variable of a literal type such as double.

p68.why: A class cannot contain a member of its own incomplete type.

p69.why: The in-class initializer of a const static int must be a constant expression, and n is not.

p70.why: A static data member cannot have the name of the class.

p71.why: Two data members cannot have the same name.

p72.why: A static data member can be thread_local.

p73.why: A default member initializer sees later members.

p74.why: An lvalue call picks the & overload and an rvalue call picks the && overload.

p75.why: limit is a const int with a constant initializer, so the local class can read its value.

p76.why: Members have increasing addresses in declaration order.

p77.why: A static member function cannot be virtual.

p78.why: A member type alias cannot have the name of the class.

p79.why: Two distinct complete objects have distinct addresses.

p80.why: An empty class has a size greater than zero.

p81.why: The explicit object parameter must be the first parameter.

p82.why: The prvalue initializes self directly; Clang 18 rejects because Fixed has no usable copy or move, and the other compilers run it and exit 0.

p83.why: A static member function cannot have a ref-qualifier.

p84.why: Clang and GCC reject a default argument on an explicit object parameter, and EDG accepts it.

p85.why: A data member must have a complete type.

p86.why: A non-static data member cannot be thread_local.

p87.why: The same member function cannot be declared twice.

p88.why: The static data member has no definition in either unit, so the linker fails.

p89.why: A const member cannot be mutable.

p90.why: A local class cannot define a friend function.
